players.product: Inference-first GPU-as-a-Service cloud on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs deployed in colocation sites; NVIDIA Cloud Partner

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus customer concentration (customers not named): in Q1 2026 three customers accounted for approximately 79% of total revenues (Customer A 24%, Customer B 44%, Customer F 11%; Q1 2025: three customers approximately 92%). In 2025 two customers accounted for approximately 67% (Customer A 36%, Customer B 31%); in 2024 four customers accounted for approximately 100%. Approximately 99% of Q1 2026 hosting revenue came from two customers, and approximately 100% of 2025 hosting revenue from three customers.
quarterly_data.figure: three customers approximately 79% of Q1 2026 revenue; two customers approximately 67% of 2025 revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus: a majority of QumulusAI's GPUaaS revenue is generated through RunPod Inc., its largest channel partner, which manages orchestration and customer acquisition for QumulusAI's servers on its platform; revenue is shared on an 80% QumulusAI / 20% RunPod basis under RunPod's standard service terms. RunPod contributed 85.7% of GPUaaS revenue for April 1 through December 31, 2025 and 71.9% for Q1 2026 (it accounted for 95% of The Cloud Minders' GPUaaS revenue in 2024). RunPod was QumulusAI's significant HPC client in 2025 and Q1 2026; QumulusAI says it is working to increase the proportion of direct enterprise customers.
quarterly_data.figure: RunPod 71.9% of Q1 2026 GPUaaS revenue (85.7% for April-December 2025); 80% / 20% revenue share

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus customer contracts on NVIDIA Blackwell nodes (customers not named): on May 11, 2026 a customer subscribed to 128 bare metal clustered NVIDIA B300 GPU nodes for a three-year term with aggregate contracted fees of approximately $99.6 million (upfront payment approximately $16.9 million); on May 28, 2026 a customer subscribed to 32 bare metal clustered NVIDIA B200 GPU nodes for a three-year term with aggregate contracted fees of approximately $24.8 million (upfront payment approximately $4.9 million).
quarterly_data.figure: 128 B300 nodes, approximately $99.6 million over three years; 32 B200 nodes, approximately $24.8 million over three years

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus capacity and suppliers: QumulusAI operates in colocation data centers in Marietta (Georgia), Kansas City (Missouri), Denver (Colorado) and Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) with combined deployed and contracted capacity of approximately 7 MW; it has secured rights of first refusal for 15 MW of IT load capacity and is planning expansion exceeding 120 MW of total IT load, with potential to support over 90,000 NVIDIA B200/B300 GPUs. It works with data center operators Coresite, H5 and Nocix to deploy AI-ready infrastructure, and coordinates with hardware vendors Super Micro Computer, Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Lenovo and Gigabyte, whose systems integrate NVIDIA GPUs. Deposits (prepayments to suppliers and manufacturers to purchase compute power and related equipment at a preset price) were $19,908,940 at March 31, 2026 versus $13,622,641 at December 31, 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 7 MW deployed and contracted; ROFR for 15 MW; expansion planned exceeding 120 MW; equipment deposits $19,908,940

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus revenue mix: 2025 revenue was $11,845,870 (+46%), of which revenue from compute power (HPC segment) was $4,938,705 (none in 2024), mining hosting $6,090,970 and cryptocurrency mining $816,195. Q1 2026 revenue was $3,419,918 (+83%), including compute power revenue of $2,102,512. QumulusAI licenses hosted.ai software to manage GPU resource allocation, scheduling and access, with fees from $10,000 per month for up to 64 NVIDIA B200 level GPUs up to $168,000 per month at 256 or more.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 compute power revenue $4,938,705; Q1 2026 compute power revenue $2,102,512
